Performance

httpjet is fast — and these docs are strict about where the time goes. Every figure names its regime, because a loopback benchmark (synthetic, on-box, PGO build) is not the same thing as production telemetry (real CDN-fronted traffic). The historical production samples describe one site and traffic mix; they are not a prediction for every deployment.

Read the regime, not just the number

loopback benchmark · synthetic, on-box, PGO production telemetry · real CF-fronted traffic hardware counters · perf at saturation

Loopback removes the external network and CDN, but a test may still include TLS handshakes. It isolates a particular workload for comparison. No loopback figure here is a production capacity number. Origin telemetry describes the sampled requests at the server; it does not measure the complete browser-to-edge journey.

Where the time actually goes

Where a production request spends its time

live sample · 2026-08-30 · mean request 9.99 ms

The LSAPI interval is elapsed time, including backend wait, not PHP CPU time. Rewrite and cache lookup account for 0.09% of this sample mean.

table view
milliseconds
LSAPI time to first byte (backend wait)8.96 ms
everything else (TLS, h2, rewrite 5.4 µs, cache lookup 3.2 µs, log)1.03 ms
⎁
Measured

In the historical production samples, LSAPI response time accounted for 86.5–98.8% of measured request wall time. That interval includes waiting for the backend and is not a measure of PHP CPU time. In the June 2026 telemetry httpjet's own request phases were about 0.2% — roughly 138 µs per request (rewrite, cache lookup, compression); a synthetic cache hit costs ~38 µs of CPU including TLS, HTTP/2, rewrite, cache lookup and access logging. The 2026-08-30 sample: mean request 9.99 ms, 8.96 ms of it LSAPI TTFB, rewrite 5.4 µs, cache lookup 3.2 µs; pool acquire p99.9 < 1 ms.

production telemetry · --telemetry-file + --php-slow-log

These observations point to backend response time and cacheability as useful areas to investigate for that workload. CPU time, elapsed latency, and cache-hit performance are different measurements; one cannot be converted directly into another.

At the instruction floor. Saturated h2 hits show IPC 1.55, 0.31% branch-miss, 1.6 L1d misses per 100 instructions. Instructions per request bottleneck, not locality. Futex (~85% of syscall time) was idle parking, not contention. Box sat ~50% idle at ceiling.

Responses: global mimalloc, on-core fast path plus memo. October 2026 campaign (0.0.9–0.1.5): skip double lookup for 404/PHP GETs (−14.5% cookied CPU); memoize .htaccess matches (access_decision_for_request 13% → 2.7%); --trusted-proxy-idle-secs 1800 (handshakes −30% x86, −78% ARM); --page-cache-dict-level (ARM encode ~50% → 11%); pool buffers via hj_core::recycle::BODY_BUFS under MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0.

Release 0.1.10: controlled A/B against 0.1.5

The 0.1.10 release (October 26, 2026) closed the five-round review. It found 23 issues, fixed 22, and closed 1 by decision. The full workspace suite (3,068 tests) stayed green. Both builds ran back to back here. Each used its production flags. The run covered 16 workloads, 5 blocks, in both run orders. The report classified 0 of 80 metric rows as worse beyond the test’s noise thresholds. Some point estimates moved in the unfavorable direction, as shown below. Every figure is a relative A/B change.

Honest caveats

Static-file CPU per request is up 1–2%, which is within the measurement noise. The h2 cache-hit p99 row (+20%) is a high-variance metric on a loop that finishes in a couple of milliseconds. The largest page-cache miss and warmer gains come mostly from the egress-at-rest work that shipped in 0.1.7, which 0.1.5 predates.

Vs 0.1.9 alone, CPU/request: PHP −4.7%, beacon −4.3%, cookied serves −4.2%, h2 hits −1.8%. HPACK encode 4.73 µs → 1.34 µs (Huffman + memo). Cookie SetEnvIf 29 µs → 1 µs (linear lookahead).

Also fixes sandbox 404s: RestrictSUIDSGID=yes makes openat2 return ENOSYS. No-follow walk now resolves docroots. Transient unit: 0.1.9 404, 0.1.10 200.

Release 0.1.11: two defaults flipped on

0.1.11 (November 7, 2026) defaults two optimizations on: coop ring (--uring-ring coop; legacy/defer selectable) and response memo for public hits (off: --no-page-cache-response-memo; old opt-in still parses). ARM already ran both. x86 ran neither.

~908k h2 static figure unchanged. aarch64 coop alone neutral vs legacy. Memo retains cookieless public GETs only, exact freshness/Age/purge fences. Gates pre-flip: 40 memo tests, purge-revocation test, 24 H1/H2 + 4 H3 real-hit arms.

Also removes Beeper/eBPF experiment code. Adopts ARM canary for voidrune. Clears H1/H3 panic-ratchet sites. Packaging fixes (musl, H3 stack, Gentoo DIGESTS) change no serving behavior.

0.2.7 dedicated lab benchmarks

The November 26, 2026 run measured 0.2.7 (on-core monoio LSAPI for HTTP/1.1 & HTTP/2 PHP, borrowed H2 memo hints, pre-rendered CLF log prefixes, single-inline H2 flushes, and reusable write_watch::Slot H1 write timers) with Unified PGO on a dedicated VM. All 1,710,000 sweep requests succeeded across eight workloads and three rounds, plus php-h2 (50.6k req/s) and wrk H1 (416.6k req/s) in the extended sweep, with 0.44 minor faults / 1k req on perf stat.

Because separate GCE VMs can shift baseline numbers by ~10%, we also ran a same-VM 10-round matched PGO sweep (73.5M requests, 0 errors): 0.2.7 beat 0.2.6 on every workload — PHP H1 +32.3% (p99 −33.2%), Cached H2 +20.5% (p99 −19.3%), PHP H2 +17.9% (p99 −33.7%), Static H2 +13.6% (p99 −34.2%), Empty H2 +12.7% (p99 −37.6%), and Rewrite-heavy H2 +10.0% (p99 −17.8%).

Release 0.2.4: transport, pipeline, and backend optimizations (Waves 1–11)

0.2.4 (November 20, 2026) ships 11 waves of hot-path performance work and 36 reliability fixes across transport, page cache, rewrite, proxy, and lifecycle paths. Verification: 3,237 workspace tests green, panic-lint ratchet down to 567 sites (from 572), 15/15 release functional checks pass, wire and flags unchanged.

  • Transport & framing (H1/H2/H3): stack-local zero-map fast path for single-frame H2 requests; small-body coalescing into inline/head buffers across H1, H2, and H3; direct HPACK and QPACK encoding without scratch copies; compile-time QPACK static lookup; single-pass HPACK static/dynamic lookups; inherited listener TCP socket options.
  • fast_memo & request pipeline: shared Arc<HeaderMap> zero-clone fast_memo egress across H1/H2/H3; 50 ms coarse HTTP Date clock cache; single-probe router host resolution; compact IPv4/IPv6 ACL bitmask tables with a 16-slot reload-safe TLS peer cache; cached static RootDir descriptors with FxHash metadata lookups.
  • Rewrite, compression & backends: borrowed zero-alloc header and path lookups across .htaccess and mod_rewrite evaluation; pooled plain-zstd and streamed-gzip codecs; borrowed LSAPI CGI builders and zero-alloc log escaping.

Release 0.2.3: progressive stream-fill, single-encode zstd, buffered-work slicing

0.2.3 (November 16, 2026) added progressive stream-fill for unframed cacheable misses (streaming to the client while a backend-paced task stores at the end), single-encode streamed zstd caching, --buffered-work-min-bytes (64 KiB yielding slices for large buffered encodes), borrowed static fast-path request heads, ordered proxy-pool idle expiry, lazy PHP slow-log record identity, and a dependency refresh (aws-lc-rs 1.19, brotli 9.1.3, zstd-safe 8.3, io-uring 0.7.16, openssl 0.10.82, nix 0.32). In the 2026-11-21 lab sweep, 0.2.3 vs 0.2.2 moved H2 1 KiB 794.6k → 849.1k (+6.9%) and page-cache hits 679.3k → 720.3k (+6.0%), with H1 static (378.8k → 383.4k), heavy .htaccess (672.6k → 656.9k H2, 341.6k → 343.1k H1), and PHP/LSAPI (39.6k → 39.6k) flat within round spread.

Release 0.2.1 / 0.2.2: admission fix, second review pass

0.2.1 (2026-11-12) sized the page-cache store-admission filter so a never-requested URL reads zero — --page-cache-admit-threshold 2 had decayed into storing every cacheable response — kept LSAPI length-prefix guards in release builds, and added fuzz targets. 0.2.2 (2026-11-12) closed a QUIC flood-guard bypass (a second datagram re-servicing the handshake slot), re-parses access files on ctime/size/inode change, asks proxied upstreams for identity under subFilter, drops refused ACME orders, and cuts the admission filter's false positives. Neither release shipped hot-path work, and the lab shows it: 0.2.1 vs 0.2.0 and 0.2.2 vs 0.2.1 are flat within round spread on every workload.

Lab VM, 2026-11-12 (loopback, server on 4 vCPUs, loadgen on 4, every release PGO-built from its tag, 3 rotated rounds, median; all thirteen releases re-measured in this one run). Release 0.2.0: security audit fixes and cold-start latency

0.2.0 (November 11, 2026) is the result of a security and robustness review of everything added since 0.1.10. It fixes 20+ issues, each with a regression test, and changes one startup behaviour you can measure: the .htaccess chain is parsed once, before the first connection, and its rewrite prefilter is built off the request path. Before, every serving thread parsed the same 900-line file after each restart, reload or edit, and requests stalled for the parse (about 0.5 s of CPU).

  • Cold start: slowest request of a 64-way burst right after boot 508 ms → 3 ms; httpjet check --strict on the production config 1.5 s → 0.07 s. Gate: scripts/cold_start_latency_test.sh.
  • Security and correctness: upstream WebSocket handshake validation; no credentials in capsule revalidation; every gzip member of a backend response decoded; out-of-order LSAPI packets refused; control characters escaped in the text error log; a QUIC Initial that closes itself no longer leaves a connection behind for 60 s; shared cache bodies no longer drain the server-wide HTTP/3 body budget; listener CPU steering only where the NIC has a receive queue per worker.
  • Observability: httpjet_h2_conn_ends_total{reason}, httpjet_pagecache_ghost_hits_total, httpjet_htaccess_parses_total.
  • Verification: 3,171 workspace tests, h2spec 146/146 over TLS, memo parity 192 cells with zero diffs, HPACK and HTTP/1 fuzzers clean for 14 million runs. No flags change; the wire is unchanged.

Honest caveats

The production-host rows share a machine with live traffic, and the same servers swing ±10–20% between runs there: nginx's H2 1 KiB moved from 180,940 (2026-11-08) to 153,485 (this run) with no change on its side. Read them as the shape of the comparison, not as a precise delta against 0.1.12. The lab table, where both builds ran back to back on an idle VM, is the version-to-version comparison. The 0.1.12 dedicated load-generator table below was not re-run for 0.2.0 and still describes 0.1.12. The cache rows used a non-forum /help/ page through the real origin cache (metrics endpoint not verified in this run; each page was primed and confirmed as x-litespeed-cache: hit). Raw CSVs for this run are on the benchmark page.

Release 0.1.12: hot-path allocation and contention reductions

0.1.12 (November 8, 2026) cuts hot-path allocation/contention: borrowed routing (Router::resolve_ref), single-pass header scan, HPACK name reuse, batched IDs, cached dates, sharded counters, diskstore/metablob refinements, lighter logging. No flags change. Wire unchanged. Parity gate: 192 cells, zero diffs.

The origin cache result

Largest real-workload fact: the origin page cache. Each hit replaces a PHP render with a memory/tmpfs copy.

One forum page: cache hit vs full PHP render

HTTPS loopback · PGO · 152 KB page · req/s

≈40× the throughput, ≈17× lower p50 latency. The cache removes the backend from the request entirely. Source: bench-results/httpjet-cache-run1.csv

table view
requests / s

2026-08-30 refresh, real /help/* hits, shared host: ~5.4k req/s h2, ~6.7k h1. Hit ratio reads low structurally: ~51% of GET-200s are one-shot bot crawls beyond any TTL. Lever there: edge TTL.

At the instruction floor

File egress: sendfile and kTLS

File egress receipts (1 MiB bodies, c=50)

loopback · 2026-09-09 · req/s

Software kTLS on a virtual GVE NIC is the expected-negative case; --ktls=auto refuses virtual NICs for this reason.

table view
req/s
plaintext H1 sendfile4,852 rps
TLS 1.3 H1, kTLS off (rustls)3,000 rps
TLS 1.3 H1, kTLS forced on (software, virtual NIC)2,945 rps

Plain H1: bounded nonblocking sendfile(2). TLS 1.3 H1: kernel TLS only via --ktls=auto + physical tls-hw-tx-offload. Production virtual NIC: off [fixed]. Forced software kTLS measured worse. auto refuses it. Details: Protocol stacks.

The codegen tier — PGO + mimalloc

Production: PGO + mimalloc + -C target-cpu=native. scripts/build-pgo.sh (outside public export) runs instrument → loopback drive → rebuild. Load: h2 hits dominant, plus h2/h1 static, PHP. Frame pointers kept for pprof. Tuning belongs to one deployment. Build neutral artifacts separately.

!
A non-PGO benchmark is not a benchmark

Debug builds run ~5× slower. Plain release differs ~10% by layout alone. Build both sides identically, interleave runs. Harness (scripts/bench-suite.sh, scripts/bench-report.py) and CSVs stay outside public export.

Knobs that actually move production

LeverEffect
Page-cache opt-in coverage and TTLs (app side)The dominant lever: every hit removes a PHP render.
--page-cache-admit-threshold 1 with dictionariesCache on first sight when storage is cheap; watch httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real.
--cf-send-zstdHands the CDN the cheapest encoding to produce; no browser-visible change.
Fast-memo eligibility of the docroot chainIneligible chains pay full pipeline per request. Fix directives, keep memo.
--rewrite-ua-classifyCollapses UA diversity onto few outcome-cache entries.
TLS resumption & certified idle windowECDSA, AES-128-GCM, --tls-session-tickets 0, --trusted-proxy-idle-secs cut handshake CPU.
PHP: opcache, worker count, slow endpoints--php-slow-log attribution. Pool rarely bottlenecks (p99.9 < 1 ms).
